previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of mitochondrial myopathy, coronary artery disease with multiple prior stents, hypertension, and dyslipidemia was admitted for evaluation of intermittent chest pressure and worsening fatigue. The chest pressure was atypical and not accompanied by other cardiac symptoms. Initial and repeat troponin levels were negative, and ECG showed no ischemic changes. A chest X-ray revealed no acute abnormalities. The patient reported that his symptoms of fatigue and dyspnea on exertion were consistent with his chronic mitochondrial disease, which often requires monthly IV hydration. Admission labs showed mild acute kidney injury with a creatinine of 1.6 mg/dL, which improved to 1.3 mg/dL with IV fluid rehydration. During the hospitalization, the patient experienced orthostatic hypotension and symptomatic sinus bradycardia, prompting a reduction in metoprolol dose and discontinuation of diltiazem. He remained stable, asymptomatic, and was discharged home with medication adjustments, including stopping diltiazem, reducing metoprolol, and switching from Nexium to ranitidine. Follow-up with cardiology was recommended.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old man with mitochondrial myopathy, HTN, HL, CAD s/p 
multiple PCI's and stents who presents with one episode of chest 
pain at rest, labile blood pressure and orthostatic hypotension. 
 
.  
# Chest Pain: The patient has a history of known CAD and is s/p 
multiple cardiac caths in the past with with 5 stents in place. 
He provided a history of sudden onset chest pain at rest, which 
resolved with SL nitroglycerin.  He had no significant ECG 
changes and ruled out for MI with three sets of negative cardiac 
biomarkers.  He was continued on home regimen of statins, 
aspirin, and antihypertensive medications.  The patient then 
underwent an exercise stress MIBI, during which he had ___ 
chest pain which resolved in ___ minutes. ECG showed ischemic ST 
changes (1-1.5 mm) during exercise, which normalized at minute 7 
of rest. There was normal myocardial perfusion and wall motion.  
The patient's old catheterization images from ___ in ___ 
and ___ at ___ were reviewed by Dr. ___.  Although he has 
a known 70% lesion in the PDA, this lesion was deemed too 
distal/small to be amenable to further intervention.  The 
patient was extensively counseled regarding this decision, and 
the fact that he may continue to experience intermittent chest 
pain.  The patient's Imdur was increased on discharge to 30 mg 
daily.  
.  
# HTN: The patient has a history of labile blood pressure at 
prior admissions and at home.  He was initially continued on his 
home antihypertensive regimen.  At discharge he was instructed 
to increase Imdur as noted above and change to clonidine patch 
for more stable blood pressure control. He may be able to be 
titrated off clonidine as an outpatient.
.
# Orthostatic Hypotension: The patient reported symptomatic 
orthostatic hypotension at home, which he continued to 
experience in-house.  He provided a tilt-table report from 
___ in ___, which found  him to have 
""orthostatic intolerance and postural tachycardia"" consistent 
with autonomic neuropathy.  On review of OMR note from his 
neurologist, it seems that autonomic dysfunction could be 
attributed to his underlying mitochondrial disorder.  He was 
treated with IV fluids while admitted and educated about the 
chronic nature of this disorder.
.  
# Mitochondrial myopathy: Per the patient's report, he requires 
monthly admissions to the hospital for IV fluids secondary to 
his mitochondrial myopathy and renal tubular disease. He 
reported feeling slightly ""dehydrated"" at admission, and his 
creatine was slightly elevated with stable electrolytes.  He was 
treated with IV fluid rehydration and felt symptomatically 
improved at discharge.
.  
# CKD Stage II: The patient appeared at or slightly above his 
baseline with Cr 1.4 at admission (prior values from ___ range 
from 1.2-1.6, but patient most values from admissions for 
dehydration). Patient reported feeling ""slightly dehydrated"" at 
presentation, however FeNa was not suggestive of a prerenal 
etiology.  He was treated with IV fluids and Cr improved to 1.2.

nosigns or symptoms of CHF on this admission.

# RHYTHM: The patient remained in normal sinus rhythm on this 
admission and was monitored on telemetry without any significant 
arrhythmic events.
